fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Multiple Structures; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark the detached structure with its own address or unit identifier so responders can quickly distinguish it from the main residence.
• Keep the area between the main residence and detached structure clear of parked vehicles to allow responder movement between the two buildings.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm staging area near the front driveway where responding units can set down equipment without blocking vehicle movement.
• If the driveway does not allow a fire or emergency vehicle to turn around, identify and mark an alternate turnaround point on the property so responding drivers do not have to back a long distance to the road.
• Keep all walkways between the parking area and both structures clear of stored items, landscaping overgrowth, or equipment so responders can move on foot without obstruction.
• Trim any landscaped plantings that overhang or narrow the driveway approach to maintain full vehicle-width clearance.
• If the detached structure has its own access point, keep that entry unlocked or mark where a key is stored so responders do not have to force entry.
• Post a simple site map near the front entrance showing the location of both structures, access points, and utility shut-offs to help arriving responders orient quickly.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Grass Cover; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang close to or over any structure on the property.
• Thin the cluster of trees to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly next to any structure.
• Cut grass short in the open areas surrounding the structures.
• Clear ground vegetation from beneath trees to reduce the amount of connected plant material between the ground and tree canopy.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow in groups near any structure.
• Keep all access routes clear of low-hanging branches that could block a vehicle.
• Maintain the open green space by mowing regularly and removing any dead grass or plant material.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation from around the base of any structure.
